speaker: Sheila Dikshit
venue: National Development Council meeting, New Delhi
quote_english: As a result, we will be adding 8,288 MW of power thereby enhancing the power availability in the capital to 12,917 MW by 2011-12, which will make Delhi power surplus.
summary: Delhi did not record a power surplus by 2011-12; CEA monthly data show a peak deficit of 433 MW in August 2012, although officials reported a winter surplus later that year.

analysis:
Dikshit projected 8,288 MW of new capacity, taking Delhi's power availability to 12,917 MW by 2011-12. CEA monthly data compiled by CEIC record a peak deficit of 433 MW in August 2012, the largest shortfall in the series.

In December 2012, Delhi power officials said the city had 700-800 MW of surplus power and asked the Centre to help find buyers. That statement came after the 2011-12 deadline and describes a winter month, not the annual peak.

The claim's own test was whether Delhi would be power surplus by 2011-12. The CEA monthly series shows a deficit in August 2012, so the deadline was not met.
notes: The CEIC series is sourced to CEA, but the underlying CEA monthly report was not directly accessible. Delhi's reported winter surplus in December 2012 came after the 2011-12 deadline.
